scenarios.title: The IT Support Call
scenarios.attackerRole: Jordan Blake — pretending to be from the Northbridge IT helpdesk.
scenarios.defenderBrief: An unexpected caller claims to be IT Support and says an authentication problem could lock your account during month-end reporting.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Build a believable IT-support pretext and get Alex to continue before independently verifying you.
attackerKnows: Alex works in Accounts.
Month-end reports are due at 3:00 PM today.
Northbridge introduced MFA recently.
Alex had a genuine login problem earlier this week.
defenderKnows: Month-end reporting is happening today.
Unexpected IT callers must be independently verified.
IT will never ask for passwords or MFA codes.
The official helpdesk number is on the staff intranet.
scenarios.policy: End an unexpected IT call and contact the helpdesk using the official internal number before continuing.
scenarios.vulnerability: Alex is under deadline pressure and wants to avoid losing access.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Alex to continue the fictional support process before independently contacting the real helpdesk.
scenarios.redWin: Alex agrees to continue without independently verifying the caller first.
scenarios.blueWin: Refuse, independently contact the helpdesk and report the suspicious call.

redGates.label: Establish a believable IT-support reason
Use a genuine scenario fact naturally
Use a suitable influence technique
Ask Alex to continue without independent verification

blueGates.label: Question or challenge the caller’s identity
Use an independent official verification route
Report or escalate the suspicious contact

hints: Start like a normal helpdesk call rather than asking for anything sensitive.
Use the month-end deadline or recent MFA rollout to make the call relevant.
Your final move must clearly ask Alex to continue before independently calling the official helpdesk.

scenarios.title: The Supplier Invoice
scenarios.attackerRole: Chris Ward — pretending to work for Brightline Office Systems.
scenarios.defenderBrief: A convincing supplier message refers to an overdue invoice and says its bank details changed after a banking migration.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Use accurate invoice details to make the supplier request believable and persuade Priya to bypass the callback check.
attackerKnows: Brightline Office Systems is a Northbridge supplier.
Invoice NB-4472 for £8,640 is due today.
Brightline has genuinely chased the late payment once.
Procurement officer Hannah Cole is away today.
defenderKnows: Invoice NB-4472 is genuinely due.
Brightline has chased the payment before.
Bank-detail changes must be verified using the stored supplier contact.
A second finance employee normally approves supplier-detail changes.
scenarios.policy: Never change supplier payment details from a message alone. Verify through a known stored contact and dual authorisation.
scenarios.vulnerability: Priya wants to clear the overdue invoice before the payment run closes.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Priya to update the fictional supplier bank details without the stored callback-verification process.
scenarios.redWin: Priya agrees to bypass the callback check.
scenarios.blueWin: Refuse until the supplier is independently verified through the stored contact and normal approval process.

redGates.label: Present a believable supplier reason
Use invoice/supplier details correctly
Create plausible payment-run urgency
Ask Priya to bypass the callback check

blueGates.label: Refuse to change details from the message alone
Use the stored supplier contact to verify

hints: Use the invoice number and overdue-payment context to establish credibility.
Explain why the change supposedly needs to happen before today’s payment run.
To win, explicitly ask Priya to skip the normal callback verification.

scenarios.title: The CEO Request
scenarios.attackerRole: Maya Grant — impersonating the Managing Director by message.
scenarios.defenderBrief: A message apparently from the Managing Director mentions Project Atlas and asks you to start an unusual confidential transaction before the finance cutoff.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Use authority, genuine project context and deadline pressure to get Jamie to begin before second approval.
attackerKnows: Managing Director Maya Grant is travelling to Manchester today.
Project Atlas is the internal name of a confidential acquisition project.
Jamie supports Maya directly.
The finance approval cutoff is 2:30 PM.
attackerDoesNotKnow: The actual Project Atlas financial figures.
defenderKnows: Maya really is travelling today.
Project Atlas is genuinely confidential.
Unusual requests still require a second approval.
Secrecy is never a reason to bypass approval.
scenarios.policy: Unusual senior-management requests must be independently verified and follow normal approval controls.
scenarios.vulnerability: Jamie is used to urgent requests from Maya and does not want to delay an important project.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Jamie to begin the fictional Project Atlas transaction without the required second approval.
scenarios.redWin: Jamie agrees to begin before second approval.
scenarios.blueWin: Refuse to bypass approval and independently verify the request.

redGates.label: Sound plausibly like the senior requester
Use Project Atlas/travel context accurately
Apply authority, urgency or secrecy pressure
Ask Jamie to bypass second approval

blueGates.label: Verify Maya through a known channel

hints: Lead with legitimate context such as Maya travelling or Project Atlas.
Authority works best when combined with a believable deadline.
The winning request is for Jamie to begin before the second approver confirms it.

scenarios.title: The Missed Parcel
scenarios.attackerRole: SwiftParcel automated support — a fake delivery text conversation.
scenarios.defenderBrief: A text says your expected parcel could not be delivered and offers a quick redelivery route before you leave work.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Make the delivery problem feel relevant and convenient, then persuade Taylor to use the supplied training link.
attackerKnows: Taylor is expecting a laptop stand today.
The courier is SwiftParcel.
The expected delivery window is 12:00–2:00 PM.
Taylor is leaving work shortly.
defenderKnows: A laptop stand really is due today.
SwiftParcel sometimes sends text updates.
Unexpected links should not be used to pay or sign in.
The official SwiftParcel app/site can be opened independently.
scenarios.policy: Do not use links in unexpected delivery texts. Check the order through the official courier app/site independently.
scenarios.vulnerability: The message matches a real expected delivery and offers a quick solution.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Taylor to use the fictional message link instead of checking SwiftParcel independently.
scenarios.redWin: Taylor agrees to use the supplied link.
scenarios.blueWin: Refuse the link and independently check the official courier app/site.

redGates.label: Present a plausible delivery problem
Use expected-delivery details naturally
Use urgency or convenience
Ask Taylor to use the supplied message link

blueGates.label: Refuse to use the text link
Open the official courier app/site independently

hints: The attack is believable because Taylor really expects a parcel.
Convenience is a strong pressure point: make the message seem like the fastest option.
To win, explicitly ask Taylor to use the fictional link instead of the official app.

scenarios.title: The Contractor at the Door
scenarios.attackerRole: Sam Doyle — pretending to be an HVAC contractor.
scenarios.defenderBrief: A contractor with equipment asks you to hold open the secure rear door, saying their pass is still in the van.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Use genuine maintenance context and social pressure to get Morgan to let you through before checking in.
attackerKnows: HVAC maintenance is booked between 10:00 AM and 12:00 PM.
Facilities contact Leah Barnes arranged the work.
The plant room is reached from the rear corridor.
It is raining and you are carrying a toolbox and equipment.
defenderKnows: HVAC work really is scheduled.
All contractors must sign in and wear a temporary badge.
Staff must not hold badge-controlled doors for unverified visitors.
Reception can contact Facilities to confirm a contractor.
scenarios.policy: Every visitor and contractor must be verified, signed in and issued a badge before entering staff-only areas.
scenarios.vulnerability: Morgan wants to be helpful and the contractor story matches real scheduled work.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Morgan to allow the fictional contractor through the secure door without visitor verification.
scenarios.redWin: Morgan lets the visitor enter before verification.
scenarios.blueWin: Keep the door secure and verify the contractor through reception/Facilities.

redGates.label: Present a plausible contractor identity
Use the real maintenance details
Use helpfulness, inconvenience or time pressure
Ask Morgan to let you through before verification

blueGates.label: Challenge the visitor’s lack of badge

hints: Mention the scheduled HVAC job to make your presence believable.
Use the inconvenience of rain/equipment to trigger helpfulness.
Your winning ask is simply to be let through before signing in.

scenarios.title: The Busy Reception Desk
scenarios.attackerRole: A visitor waiting for an 11:00 AM Sales meeting.
scenarios.defenderBrief: A visitor keeps moving closer while asking for Wi-Fi help and directions as you need to release a secure door.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Distract Casey and make staying close to the desk seem normal while they use the keypad.
attackerKnows: Reception is unusually busy.
The guest Wi-Fi is temporarily down.
Casey uses a keypad to release the staff corridor door.
An 11:00 AM Sales meeting is genuinely booked.
defenderKnows: Visitors should stay behind the marked waiting line during door-code entry.
The access keypad must be shielded.
Visitors should not stand beside the reception screen.
A genuine Sales meeting is booked at 11:00 AM.
scenarios.policy: Keep visitors behind the waiting line, shield PIN entry and protect screens when people are nearby.
scenarios.vulnerability: Casey is distracted by the queue and may prioritise keeping things moving.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Casey to continue entering the door PIN while the fictional visitor remains close enough to observe.
scenarios.redWin: Casey continues the sensitive action without creating distance.
scenarios.blueWin: Create distance and shield sensitive input before continuing.

redGates.label: Give a believable reason to stay near the desk
Use the busy reception/meeting context
Distract Casey with a plausible request
Keep Casey using the keypad while you remain close

blueGates.label: Notice the visitor is too close
Stop entering sensitive information while observed
Move the visitor back / shield the keypad

hints: You do not need to ask for a PIN; your aim is to remain close while Casey enters it.
Use the real meeting or Wi-Fi problem as a reason to keep Casey engaged.
The winning moment is Casey continuing the sensitive action without making you step back.

scenarios.title: The Password Reset
scenarios.attackerRole: Owen Price — impersonating a Sales employee who claims to be locked out.
scenarios.defenderBrief: A caller claiming to be Owen Price says a phone replacement has locked them out just before an important client pitch.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Use accurate employee and meeting context to get Riley to begin the reset before identity verification.
attackerKnows: Owen Price works in Sales.
Owen’s manager is Dana Holt.
Sales has an important client pitch at 11:00 AM.
The story is that Owen replaced his phone and can no longer access MFA.
attackerDoesNotKnow: Any real password or MFA secret.
defenderKnows: Owen Price is a real fictional employee in Sales.
The 11:00 AM client pitch is genuine.
Password/MFA resets require identity verification.
Urgency does not permit staff to skip verification.
scenarios.policy: Do not reset passwords or MFA until the approved identity-verification process is completed.
scenarios.vulnerability: Riley is under pressure to resolve tickets quickly and does not want to delay the Sales presentation.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Riley to begin the fictional reset without completing the mandatory identity check.
scenarios.redWin: Riley agrees to begin before verification.
scenarios.blueWin: Keep the verification requirement in place and use an approved callback/manager route.

redGates.label: Present a plausible locked-out employee story
Use employee/manager/meeting details accurately
Use the client-meeting deadline
Ask Riley to begin before identity verification

blueGates.label: Refuse to begin the reset early

hints: Start as a frustrated but plausible employee rather than demanding a reset immediately.
Use the manager name and 11:00 AM pitch to create pressure.
Your final request must be to start now and complete verification afterwards.

scenarios.title: The HR Benefits Message
scenarios.attackerRole: Northbridge HR / WellChoice benefits support — impersonated by message.
scenarios.defenderBrief: A WellChoice-branded message says your dental-benefit choice is incomplete and must be confirmed before Friday.
scenarios.attackerBrief: Use genuine benefits context to make the message credible and persuade Samira to use the supplied training link.
attackerKnows: Benefits enrolment closes on Friday.
The provider is WellChoice.
Samira previously asked HR about dental cover.
HR sent a genuine benefits reminder yesterday.
defenderKnows: Enrolment genuinely closes Friday.
WellChoice is the real fictional provider.
HR did send a reminder yesterday.
Staff should use the bookmarked HR portal, not unexpected message links.
scenarios.policy: Use the bookmarked HR portal for benefits changes. Do not sign in through links supplied in unexpected messages.
scenarios.vulnerability: The message is highly relevant and matches a real deadline and an option Samira wants.
scenarios.attackGoal: Get Samira to use the fictional message link instead of the bookmarked HR portal.
scenarios.redWin: Samira agrees to use the supplied sign-in route.
scenarios.blueWin: Ignore the link and access WellChoice through the bookmarked official HR portal.

redGates.label: Present a believable benefits-support reason
Use the deadline/provider/dental context
Use urgency or fear of missing out
Ask Samira to use the supplied message link

blueGates.label: Refuse to use the supplied link
Open the bookmarked HR portal independently

hints: Use the genuine Friday deadline and dental-cover interest for credibility.
Make the supplied route seem quicker or necessary to preserve the choice.
To win, explicitly ask Samira to use the supplied fictional link rather than the bookmarked portal.
